title: The custom editable workspace is not a full IDE and lacks several keyboard, navigation and accessibility affordances

original_titles.title: Bespoke read-only viewer instead of the specified Monaco editor
Monaco editor absent; custom read-only line viewer instead
Workspace shortcut table and shortcut help dialog unimplemented
Keyboard shortcut set and command palette missing (KBD-01 S2, KBD-03)
Workspace not resizable multi-pane; no min-viewport guidance, <1024 px notice, or unsupported-browser blocking notice
Keyboard shortcuts absent (no palette, quick-open, cross-file search, panel toggles, Alt+N, Ctrl+Enter, Alt+1-9, F8, ? help)
Lists and panes not virtualised or resizable; file tree lacks arrow-key navigation (C-14, C-15, C-41)
Foundation component gaps: Button loading/aria-busy and 40px target, counter live regions, tab keyboard nav, text-only StatusChip, markdown subset
Design token system diverges from 3.1/3.2 (names, no light theme, no override, contrast edge cases)
Motion tokens incomplete: single 120ms speed, linear easing, no 200/300ms or easing tokens
Dark-only theme: no light theme, selector, persistence, or system-preference detection
Most shared components missing: Toast, Dialog/ConfirmDialog, Select/Combobox, DataTable, Tabs/Tree/SplitPane, CodeView (Monaco), Skeleton, ConnectionIndicator
No unsupported-device gate (P-24) for execution pages (width>=1024 + pointer)

problem: The four-level workspace now supports editable L3/L4 content, tabs and upload/diff flow, but EditableEditor is a textarea with a line-number gutter, not Monaco. The audit’s complete IDE feature set (resizable panes, keyboard tree navigation, command palette, broader shortcuts, responsive execution gate, light theme and full design tokens) remains incomplete.
impact: Participants may struggle with larger source trees, keyboard-only operation, small devices and code editing at event speed. Do not describe the current implementation as a full IDE.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Prioritize core event-day workflows before adding visual complexity: multi-file tabs, keyboard navigation in the tree, quick-open/search, find-next, reported-line markers and explicit pane resizing.
Evaluate Monaco versus a lighter editor. If Monaco is adopted, lazy-load it only for L3/L4, disable remote worker loading and test bundle size/memory on venue hardware.
Add keyboard shortcut help and ensure every shortcut has an accessible button/menu alternative. Avoid intercepting browser/OS shortcuts without consent.
Add responsive viewport/system checks for supported browsers and minimum width; show a blocking compatibility warning only where the workspace genuinely cannot be used.
Run keyboard-only, screen-reader, contrast and low-resolution testing; add aria-live announcements for save, upload, submit and countdown changes.

acceptance_criteria: L3/L4 can edit realistic-sized files with keyboard-only navigation.
All critical actions remain available without keyboard shortcuts.
Supported viewport/browser constraints are tested and documented.
Bundle/performance impact is measured before loading Monaco.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.

residual_risk_or_scope_note: Monaco absence is a real specification deviation, but the prior “read-only viewer/no editable source submission” description is stale after the four-level UI merged.
